entries.what_changed: Seal admitted a routing key with HeaderValue::from_str, which accepts bytes 0x80-0xFF, and then read it back with to_str().ok().unwrap_or(""). One predicate, parse_routing_key (at most 1,024 bytes of header text: visible ASCII, space, tab), is parsed once per writer, and the seal path takes the key as a parameter (the HeaderMap clone and its .expect are deleted).

entries.title: A consumer pull loops back only on settled poison and always delivers the leases its receive granted

entries.title: The descriptor cache never publishes a read that raced a write
entries.what_changed: Registry::get released the lock, awaited the store and inserted the result unconditionally, and invalidate was a bare remove. So a read fetched before a write could re-install the pre-write descriptor for a full 5 s TTL on every reader; this is the mechanism behind bug #9's flake, and it had four shapes, including a cached absence over a create. After a verbatim move to src/registry/cache.rs, DescriptorCache::fill claims a per-stream slot under a globally unique generation and publishes only if the generation is unchanged. Invalidation empties the slot under a fresh generation, the cap purge keeps recently touched slots, and recreate's loser invalidates instead of installing.

The per-stream control is green. A 3-lens adversarial review plus adjudicator found no publishing interleaving. The first cargo-mutants run left 4 survivors (< -> <= on elapsed()<ttl, and cache_len); these are killed by an explicit-now `within` predicate. New mutation owner registry_cache.
entries.edge_visible: none on the wire; readers stop seeing pre-write descriptors for up to 5 s after a write; a lost recreate costs one extra GET

CI is green on every push from 4c51ebfd onward, which is consistent with the fix but does not prove it; if the hang recurs, the 4c51ebfd watchdog dumps every thread's stack within 15 min.
